title: Evaluating research and researchers by the journal impact factor: is it better than coin flipping?
findings: This paper does not contain any findings related to religion or faith. The key finding is that using the Journal Impact Factor (JIF) to compare the merit of two scientific papers has a high probability of failure (approaching 0.5, or a coin flip), especially when the JIFs of the journals are not vastly different. This questions the validity of JIF as a reliable tool for research evaluation.
